ranking.note: Raised to P1: an assertion abort plus false-corruption startup failure leaving an assumeutxo node unrecoverable is the same class of crash/chainstate-integrity bug as #36149 and #35744.

Raised to P1: unlike the other regtest-only opcode proposals it fixes concrete consensus hazards (timewarp, quadratic sigops, 64-byte tx collisions), has broad concept support and a merged companion PR, so a decision is actively blocked on it; moved up from 9 for the same reason.
Moved up from 17: the largest measured user-facing validation speedup in the list (1.5x reindex, 1.13x IBD), ahead of smaller localized optimizations.
Moved up from 13 to sit with the other chainstate corruption-handling fixes (#35714, #36280) it is functionally adjacent to.
Moved up from 18: silent conversion of an unspendable script into an anyone-can-spend output is a fund-safety consequence, stronger than the refactor-flavoured P2s below it.
Moved up from 19: node silently stuck or aborting on block-storage I/O errors is a reliability problem of the same weight as #35714/#34132, and it needs an architectural decision that is stalling it.
Raised to P3->P2: reproducible std::terminate on a full disk is the same disk-error-handling stability family as #35003 and #35714, which are P2.
Moved down from 5: substantial latency/throughput benefit but still a draft concept proposal with no reviews and no correctness consequence, so it ranks below the corruption and crash fixes.
Moved up from 20: it removes a dual-path consensus hazard, fixes a real script-cache bypass, and is the stated prerequisite for #29491.

Moved down from 4: a mandatory-storage rewrite is consequential, but the driving benefit is external/kernel reader access and the design is paused pending unresolved WAL and parallel-reader questions.

Lowered to P2: with no activation parameters or signaling it is the same kind of proposal-evaluation work as #31989/#32247/#36122, which are P2; kept first among them as the most mature implementation.
Moved down from 6 to sit with the other regtest-only opcode proposals of equal consequence.
Grouped with the other regtest-only opcode proposals rather than interleaved with corruption and performance work.
Moved down from 10: explicitly an experimental draft accompanying the BIPs, with open wallet/PSBT bugs, so decision value is lower than the other soft-fork proposals.
Moved down from 11: the speedup is real but the work sits behind unmerged upstream secp256k1 modules and behind #32575, so it is the last actionable P2.
Moved up from 35: demonstrated reproducible chain loss on -reindex when xor.dat is missing is the strongest problem in the P3 band.
Moved up from 30 to lead the localized-performance P3 group (measured IBD and assumeutxo gains).
Lowered to P3: a ~10% template-validation speedup benefiting miners is comparable to the other localized optimizations (#35195, #33637) already at P3, not to the IBD-wide gains at P2.
Moved down from 22: existing restart behaviour already avoids re-processing most blocks, so the incremental benefit is smaller than the other P3 fixes above it.
Moved down from 23: the payoff is for external kernel consumers rather than node validation behaviour, and the callback-versus-container design is contested.
Moved down from 24: production validation behaviour is unchanged; the concrete win is one intermittent test race plus kernel determinism.

inconsistencies: Band inconsistency among proposed consensus changes: #29247 (CAT) was P1 while #31989, #32247 and #36122 were P2 despite all being unactivated/regtest-only proposals. All are now P2; #35793 (BIP 54) alone is P1 because it fixes concrete consensus hazards and a decision is imminent.
Dependency chain: #35861 (Testnet 5) is built on #35793 and activates BIP 54 from block 1 — review #35793 first; #35861 cannot be evaluated until the BIP 54 rules settle.
Dependency chain: #32575 is stated preparation for #29491 (Schnorr batch verification) — review #32575 first.
Dependency chain: #35646 unblocks #35570's transition to value-returning validation signatures — review #35646 before #35570.
Dependency chain: #35731 builds directly on #35714 and hardens the same flush-error path — review #35714 first, then #35731 as a follow-up.

Overlapping problem area: #35003, #36049, #35714 and #34132 all change how storage/deserialization failures are surfaced (exceptions vs fatal abort vs error returns). They should be sequenced deliberately; #35003 is blocked on exactly the architectural question (exceptions at the BlockManager boundary) that the others implicitly answer.

Overlapping problem area: #33324 (reobfuscate existing block files) and #35938 (fail instead of writing a null XOR key) both concern the blocks/xor.dat lifecycle; #35938 prevents data loss and should be reviewed first.

Overlapping direction: #36000 (prefetch threads during connection) and #36244 (async block processing off the P2P thread) both restructure the block-connection concurrency model and will likely conflict; a concept decision on the target architecture should come before detailed review of either.
Same umbrella effort: #35906, #36066 and #35569 are all steps toward the stateless validation library in #35904. Review order #35906 (defines the interfaces) then #36066 then #35569.

Category boundary: #35187 and #35557 are primarily libbitcoinkernel API additions and #35751 is primarily block-template validation; they touch validation but a reviewer may want them judged under kernel/mining. #32427 likewise is motivated by kernel/external-indexer needs while rewriting mandatory block storage — that split is worth flagging to the author.
result.notes: The list separates cleanly into four crash/consensus-integrity items (P1), a large P2 band mixing disk-error correctness, IBD performance and unactivated soft-fork proposals, a P3 band of localized speedups and internal hardening, and a small P4 tail of pure janitorial refactors. The main global correction was normalizing the proposed-opcode PRs into one band and lifting the assumeutxo/pruning crash fixes above them.
